To: Marketing Team
Date: April 9
Subject: Team lunch moved to Friday

Hello everyone,

Rosa

passages.text: Millbrook — After three years of construction, the Harrison Bridge opened to traffic on Monday morning. The new bridge, which crosses the Millbrook River, replaces an older structure that had been closed since a safety inspection found serious cracks in 2021. Mayor Ellen Park said the bridge would cut the average commute between the north and south sides of the city by fifteen minutes. The $48 million project was funded by the state government and a local transportation tax. Drivers are advised to expect delays during the first week as traffic patterns adjust. A pedestrian and bicycle path on the east side of the bridge will open next month after landscaping is completed.

Age: Drivers must be at least twenty-one years old. Drivers under twenty-five pay a daily young driver fee.

Portland — Bluehill Roasters, a local coffee company founded eight years ago, announced yesterday that it will open a second roasting facility in the Eastport district. The new site will triple the company's production capacity and create twenty-five jobs.
"We have been turning away orders for months," said founder Adaeze Obi. "Our current roaster runs nearly around the clock, and we cannot take on new restaurant customers." Ms. Obi said the company has secured a loan from a regional bank to purchase two industrial roasters and to renovate the building, a former printing shop.
Bluehill's coffee is sold at more than sixty cafés across the state. The company also operates a small shop and tasting room on Harbor Street. Under the expansion plan, the shop will keep its current location, but its tasting room will move to the new facility. Production at Eastport is scheduled to begin in January, and the company will begin hiring in October.

Greenfield — The Saturday Farmers' Market, a popular fixture in Town Square for twenty-two years, will move to the former Hartley Hardware building starting in November. Organizers made the decision after a survey found that nearly sixty percent of vendors wanted a location that would stay open through the winter.
"Outdoor markets get quieter when the weather turns cold," said market manager Josie Brandt. "With heat and a roof, our vendors can keep selling, and customers can shop in comfort." The building has about fifty stalls, compared with thirty-five in the square, and a small kitchen where vendors can prepare samples. A parking area behind the building will hold eighty cars, which is more than double the current street parking.
The market will keep its Saturday hours, from eight to one. Starting in December, it will also open on Wednesday evenings. Vendors interested in a stall can apply online until October 15.

questions.questionText: Why is the market moving?

title: Customer review of a software tool

passages.text:
★★★★☆ Useful, but needs a better mobile version
Posted by Daniel R., verified buyer
I have been using TaskFlow for six months to manage projects with a team of ten. The main advantages are the clean design and the calendar view, which lets me see every deadline at a glance. Setting up recurring tasks is simple, and the reporting tool saves me about two hours every Friday.
My main complaint concerns the mobile app. It runs slowly, and some features, such as file attachments, are missing. I also wish the notifications were easier to customize, because I get too many alerts during meetings. Customer support is responsive, though, and they answered my questions within a day.
Overall, I would recommend TaskFlow to small teams who mostly work on computers. If the company improves the app, I would give it five stars.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Riverton General Hospital announced today that its new surgical wing will be named after Dr. Samuel Achebe, who served as chief surgeon for thirty-four years. The wing, which is scheduled to open on September 1, includes eight operating rooms and a recovery area with forty beds.
"Dr. Achebe trained more than two hundred surgeons during his career," said hospital director Louise Marchetti. "We are honored to recognize his commitment to our community." The project cost $62 million, of which $15 million came from private donations. The new rooms feature advanced imaging equipment that will allow doctors to perform some operations through smaller incisions, shortening recovery times.
A public ceremony will take place on August 28 at 10 a.m. Parking will be available at the nearby Millstream Mall, with free shuttle service to the hospital. For media inquiries, contact Kyle Brandt at 555-0123.

Beginning February 1, the company will adopt two changes. First, we will move from a formal dress code to a smart-casual dress code. Second, we will offer flexible start times between 7:30 and 10:00 a.m., provided that all employees are present during core hours of 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
Flexible hours must be agreed in advance with your team leader to ensure that every department is covered. A short survey will be sent out in March to collect feedback on both changes. We believe that these updates will improve morale while maintaining our professional standards.

Baker Publishes First Recipe Book
Elena Moretti, owner of Moretti's Bakery in Dunmore, will publish her first recipe book next month. Titled Daily Bread, the book includes sixty recipes for breads, rolls and pastries, many of which are inspired by her grandmother's cooking in northern Italy. Ms. Moretti, who opened her bakery fifteen years ago, said she hopes the book will encourage people to bake at home.
A launch event will be held at the bakery on Saturday, October 12, from two to five. Ms. Moretti will sign copies and hold a baking demonstration at three. Tickets are free, but guests must reserve a place by calling the bakery. The book will be available in local bookstores and online for $24.
